body:
`auto_redirect_decision` reads the session counter and compares it with `>`
BEFORE incrementing (cps/oauth_auto_redirect.py:138-141), so counts 0, 1, 2
and 3 all initiate an OAuth start: four, not the three the constant names.
`render_login` applies the same `>` reading (cps/web.py:2621-2626).

Not a bypass and not a lockout: the counter is cleared on logout
(cps/logout.py:24) and on a successful OAuth callback (cps/oauth_bb.py:1005),
and the fall-through renders the login page normally. The defect is that the
constant misdescribes the limit, so anyone tuning it reasons off a number
that is one lower than the behaviour.

Fix is either `>= MAX_LOGIN_REDIRECTS` at both sites or a rename that states
the off-by-one. Both sites must change together or the guard and the counter
disagree.

Surfaced while reviewing #1488 (explicit OAuth auto-forward setting), which
makes this path reachable for installs that keep standard login enabled, so
more deployments will exercise it. Predates that PR; deliberately not widened
into it.
title: MAX_LOGIN_REDIRECTS=3 permits four automatic OAuth starts
